src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx:588-594 comment says a min size wins over a max size in CSS, so the minimums are capped at 100%. CSS 2.1 §10.4 resolves a conflict (min-width greater than max-width) in favour of min-width, so the statement is correct. Traced input: min-width 300px, max-width 100% in a 200px containing block gives used width 300px. The code caps minWidth with min(Npx, max(100%, 50vw)) and minHeight likewise, so in the normal case (containing block is the viewport) min <= 100% = max and the cap prevents overflow. The comment openly says that inside a small transformed ancestor the 50vw/50dvh floor can still exceed 100%. That is a stated trade-off and consistent with the claim, which is only about min beating max.

ChatWidget.tsx:591-592 set minWidth `min(Npx, max(100%, 50vw))` and minHeight `min(Npx, max(100%, 50dvh))`: capped by the containing block (100%) with a 50vw/50dvh floor. These are inline React styles, so a browser that rejects dvh drops that declaration. No stylesheet min-width/min-height applies to the floating window: chat.css:1020 min-width is only under .radchat-layout-sidebar, and the other min-* rules are on unrelated elements. No browserslist or browser-support statement exists in package.json or README (grep found none), so no declared support contradicts the claim.
